description: Master clock putting out eighteen divisions and multiples of one tempo at once, plus six ramps running across the longer spans, in any time signature from 2 to 16 beats

params.text: Sets the tempo, doubling for each unit of travel: 7.5BPM at fully counter-clockwise, 120BPM at the 0 position and 240BPM at fully clockwise
Sets how many beats a measure has, 2 to 16; changing it restarts every clock
Sets the note value one beat counts as, the bottom number of the time signature: 2 for a half note, 4 for a quarter, 8 for an eighth, 16 for a sixteenth; changing it restarts every clock
Moves the second half of each beat later or earlier, -1 to 1, the centre giving an even beat; it reaches the eighth, sixteenth and offbeat quarter outputs
Bends the six ramp outputs from nearly logarithmic at -0.99, through a straight line at 0, to exponential at 0.99
Sets how much of its own cycle each pulse output stays high, 1% to 99%
Returns every clock to the start of its cycle
Starts and stops the whole clock; while it is stopped every output stays at 0V and the clocks are held at their reset point

inputs.text: Added to the BPM knob, doubling the tempo for every volt
An external clock: each rise past 1V counts as one beat, and the tempo is taken from the average of the last four gaps, which replaces the BPM knob and its jack altogether
A rise past 1V returns every clock to the start of its cycle, and a cable here replaces the Reset button
Each rise past 0.9V starts or stops the clock, and a cable here replaces the Run button
Divided by 5 and added to the Pulse Width knob, the total clamped between 1% and 99%

outputs.text: A 10V pulse 0.08 seconds long each time the clock starts and each time it stops
A 10V pulse 0.08 seconds long each time the clock is reset
A pulse on every beat, the clock every other output is divided from
Four pulses in each beat, the offbeat ones moved by Swing
Two pulses in each beat, the second of them moved by Swing
A pulse every three quarters of a beat, free-running rather than pulled back at the bar line
One pulse in each beat, halfway through it, moved by Swing
Three pulses in the time of two beats
Three pulses in each measure
Two pulses in each measure; on an odd number of beats the first part takes the extra beat, so five beats split three then two
One pulse at the start of every measure
One pulse every four measures
One pulse every number of measures equal to the beats in a measure, so every eight measures in 8/8
One pulse every sixteen measures
One pulse every number of measures equal to the beats multiplied by the note value, so every sixteen measures in 4/4
A ramp from 0V to 10V across each half measure, bent by the Curve knob
A ramp from 0V to 10V across each measure, bent by the Curve knob
A ramp from 0V to 10V across each four measures, bent by the Curve knob
A ramp from 0V to 10V across as many measures as there are beats in one, bent by the Curve knob
A ramp from 0V to 10V across each sixteen measures, bent by the Curve knob
A ramp from 0V to 10V across the beats multiplied by the note value in measures, bent by the Curve knob
A pulse every three eighths of a beat, its cycle pulled back to the start of every measure
A pulse every three quarters of a beat, its cycle pulled back to the start of every measure
A pulse every two beats, its cycle pulled back to the start of every measure
Three pulses in the time of two beats, the cycle pulled back to the start of every measure
A pulse every beat and a half, its cycle pulled back to the start of every measure

notes: the clock comes up stopped, and nothing leaves any output until Run is pressed or a cable in the Run jack takes it high
the two displays read the tempo in beats per minute and the time signature the Beats and Quaver knobs set
the measure-bound outputs restart at every bar line, so a division that does not fit the bar begins again rather than carrying its offset into the next one
every output is monophonic and every pulse output is 10V while it is high
